title: Export as ZIP README names the site's real old address and, for WordPress, the WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL constants that otherwise keep a moved site on Tracy
steps: S1: From the TCH checkout run: node --test --test-reporter=tap packages/fleet/tracy-fleet-operation/test/backup-export.test.mjs
S2: Record the exit code, the '# tests', '# pass', '# fail' lines and the result of each case whose name starts with one of the run.tests entries.
expect: S1 exits 0 with '# fail 0' and '# pass' equal to '# tests'.

WordPress: the packaged README names the WP_HOME address read from the packaged wp-config.php as the old address, uses it in the wp search-replace command, tells the reader to set WP_HOME and WP_SITEURL to the new address, says the package is a copy of the site that does not include files over 50 MB and symbolic links, and that manifest.json gives the size limit and says how many links were left out (never that it lists them), says nothing is needed if the site stays on Tracy, offers phpMyAdmin import, and limits the DNS step to a domain that points at Tracy now.
Joomla: with $live_site set, the README names it as the old address; without it, the README says the old address is the Tracy address starting with https://<label>. and not the customer's own domain.
EmDash: the README names EMDASH_SITE_URL as the setting to change; with TRACY_EXPORT_SITE_URL it names that address as the old address, without it the fallback wording.

The old address ignores PHP comments (//, #, /* */) while keeping // inside string literals, accepts WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL only from a define( that starts a line and $live_site only from the property line, never from text inside a string literal, and the first live define wins: a commented-out or quoted address is never named.

All three READMEs say, right after the backup paragraph, to install the package into an empty folder and, for WordPress and Joomla, an empty database (EmDash names no database to create; never that installing it replaces whatever is at that place), and that changes made to another copy of the site (such as the original site after import: orders, comments, sign-ups, posts) are not in it and are lost if the package is put in place of it.
evidence: 19/10/2026, throwaway WordPress 6 + MariaDB 11 in Docker with WP_HOME/WP_SITEURL = https://lantern.tracy.site in wp-config.php (as render_wp_config.py writes them): after the old README's step 5 (wp search-replace to http://localhost:18089) the DB home/siteurl were the new address but home_url() stayed https://lantern.tracy.site and /wp-login.php answered 302 to https://lantern.tracy.site/wp-admin/. Setting the two constants as the new README says gave 200 on /, /wp-login.php and /?p=4.
fence: The README only reads the packaged configuration; the package's other members and the database placeholders are unchanged.

tests: export-package: EmDash includes app, database, uploads and its Node-host README
export-package: Joomla README names the old address from $live_site
export-package: Joomla package has move instructions and the four database placeholders
export-package: the old address ignores PHP comments
export: a full WordPress point becomes one zip
export with include-large: files over 50 MiB captured with the fresh backup are included
